goals: Mechanistic: quantify how elevation controls snowmelt-onset DOY across the Naches
Validation: compare simulated SWE / melt timing against the 6 in-domain SNOTEL stations

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM simulates SWE and melt in the default history output; SNOTEL SWE exists in-domain for validation. Snow is a fast state, so melt timing does not require long spin-up.

answerable: Melt-onset DOY and peak-SWE validation at each SNOTEL location (co-located), with expected ridgetop underestimation from 12 km averaging
Coarse elevation control on melt onset ACROSS stations separated by >12 km, since NLDAS delivers orographically-varying precip/temperature between cells

not_answerable.aspect: Local lapse rate / melt-onset difference between stations on the same ridge (<12 km apart)
not_answerable.why: NLDAS-2 is 0.125deg (~12 km) with no within-cell lapse rate; near-neighbor stations share a forcing cell, so no physically-driven melt difference can arise between them

sampling_strategy.approach: observation-pinned validation + light stratified exploratory transect
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 6 validation columns are fixed by the 6 SNOTEL stations. 4 exploratory columns placed in DISTINCT NLDAS cells across the elevation range characterize the forcing-resolved (>12 km) elevation gradient in melt onset — the mechanism the stack CAN represent — kept small because forcing, not local heterogeneity, dominates melt timing and NLDAS resolution caps the achievable elevation resolution.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Validation columns pinned to SNOTEL coordinates. Exploratory columns spread along the low-to-high elevation axis but forced to lie in separate 12 km NLDAS cells, so each samples genuinely different forcing rather than sub-grid duplicates.
sampling_strategy.replication: None beyond the natural SNOTEL clustering; near-neighbor SNOTEL pairs are retained deliberately to DEMONSTRATE the sub-12 km non-resolution rather than to test lapse rate.

sampling_plan.reason: One column co-located at each of the 6 SNOTEL stations to validate simulated SWE and melt-onset DOY against measured SWE.
Span low/mid/high elevation in separate 12 km forcing cells to characterize the coarse, forcing-resolved elevation control on melt onset that the stack can actually represent.

validation_design.target_variable: peak SWE and snowmelt-onset DOY (derived from H2OSNO / QSNOMELT)
validation_design.comparison: co-located — each simulated column at a station cell compared to that station's SWE time series; melt onset = date SWE begins sustained decline from peak
validation_design.metric: bias & RMSE on peak SWE; bias (days) on melt-onset DOY

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 default forcing (elevation-varying at 12 km), native SSURGO soil, multi-year forcing window from 1980-2018 to sample interannual melt-timing variability

requires_capabilities.capability: elevation-downscaled / sub-12 km forcing (within-cell lapse rate)
requires_capabilities.why: Stations on the same ridge are <12 km apart and share an NLDAS cell; resolving the local lapse-rate control on melt onset requires forcing that varies below 12 km
requires_capabilities.blocks: the same-ridge local-lapse-rate objective — the primary sharpened sub-goal

requires_capabilities.why: Brief does not provide station coordinates or elevations; concrete column placement and co-located comparison require them
requires_capabilities.blocks: enumeration of exact validation column lat/lon and station elevations

requires_capabilities.capability: melt-onset DOY diagnostic from SWE time series
requires_capabilities.why: Melt onset must be derived consistently from H2OSNO/QSNOMELT for both model and SNOTEL

assumptions: Multi-year forcing windows will be used so melt-onset DOY reflects interannual variability, not a single year
SNOTEL stations lie within CONUS NLDAS coverage (they do — Washington Cascades)
Ridgetop SWE underestimation from 12 km averaging is expected and will be reported, not corrected
open_questions: Which SNOTEL station pairs fall inside the same NLDAS cell? (determines how bluntly the same-ridge objective fails)
Are exact SNOTEL coordinates and station elevations available for co-location?
Preferred melt-onset definition: first sustained SWE decline, or a fixed SWE-fraction threshold?
